title: 75% of Employees Lose Focus During Online Meetings
paragraphs: Online meetings have become a normal part of working life. But according to a new survey from Australia, many people are not really paying attention during them.
The survey was carried out by people2people Recruitment, a recruitment company. It asked more than 1,200 people about their experiences in virtual meetings.

The results showed that 75% of people stop paying full attention during online meetings every time or often. Only 8% said they never lose focus. In addition, 61% said that at least half of the people in a typical online meeting seem to be doing other things at the same time.
So, what do people do when they stop paying attention? About 40% said they browse the internet, while 32% said they do other work. Another 6% check their messages, and 22% said they do nothing else.

There were several reasons why people lost focus. The most common reason, chosen by 39% of people, was that the meeting was not relevant to them. Other reasons were that meetings were too long, at 29%, or that there were too many meetings, at 23%. Only 9% blamed notifications on their devices.

Interestingly, older workers were more likely to lose focus than younger workers. Around 59% of Gen X workers and baby boomers said they lose focus at every meeting, compared with 46% of millennials and 31% of Gen Z.

Suhini Wijayasinghe, an HR expert at people2people Recruitment, said the problem is about how meetings are designed, not just about people's attention spans. When people do not pay attention, information can be missed and decisions can take longer.
The report suggests that companies should hold fewer, shorter meetings with clearer plans and fewer people. It also recommends sharing more updates in writing instead of always holding a meeting.
